A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intermittency indices of directed percolations are related to its fractal dimension and the critical exponents of directed percolating clusters.
intermittency in directed percolation is a real phenomenon, but it is much weaker than in the case of multi-particle production in high energy physics.
the cluster structure at the critical point is not homogeneous and the cluster fluctuations can be described in a self-similar way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intermittency analysis can be successfully used in the context of percolation and other related models.
directed percolation is a natural candidate for the study of intermittency-related phenomena in the context of critical phenomena.
the intermittency analysis is a powerful tool to study the fluctuations of critical clusters in the presence of boundary effects.
